messages:
Sofia: Quick follow-up on the token-claim braid refactor — trying to lock down the handoff contract between the API gateway and ingest for chunked/batched requests. I sketched a tiny proposal: https://gist.github.com/sofia/token-braid-proposal. TL;DR: gateway emits a suggested claim token header (X-Claim-Token) and fingerprint header (X-Claim-Fingerprint). Ingest can accept, reconcile, or canonicalize. Main question: how do we behave on partial uploads / header loss during retries? /cc @ingest-bot

Raj: Ran into this last week when a mobile client retried without headers and we double-credited. :grimacing: If gateway emits claim_id but retry loses header, ingest should try to re-derive claim via fingerprint and map to canonical id. But need clear semantics for who owns the ledger id.

Lena: I'd prefer ingest to own the canonical claim assignment. Gateway can propose (optimistic) but ingest decides final claim_id. Keeps ledger ownership inside ingest and avoids split-brain. Downside: ingest must be able to resolve fingerprint -> canonical_id quickly on the hot path.

Tom: Concern: offline/legacy clients may never include headers. Fallback must be robust: fingerprinting + ephemeral lease sounds reasonable. Do we have the tokenlineage fingerprint work we can reuse?

Sofia: Proposal refinement: gateway sets both X-Claim-Token (optional) and X-Claim-Fingerprint (required for chunked flows). Ingest will: 1) try to hydrate X-Claim-Token if present, 2) if missing or unknown, attempt fingerprint lookup for canonical claim_id, 3) if still missing, create new canonical claim_id and respond with header X-Claim-Resolved: <id> (202/accepted semantics for async finalization). Gateway will attach X-Claim-Resolved on subsequent retries. That avoids extra sync in happy path and makes retries idempotent.

Raj: OK but audit concerns: if ingest can reassign claim_id, provenance must capture original gateway/request identity. We should include a compact provenance string rather than a full array to avoid schema churn. e.g. provenance=req:<id>|gw:<node>|ts:<ms>.

Lena: Agreed. Keep provenance as a single delimited string field on the envelope and ledger entries. Example: "req:abc123|gw:us-west-2-1|ts:1680000000000". We log raw envelope so we can rehydrate for audits.

Sofia: Also proposing a checkpoint message shape for chunk finalizer sent to the ingest topic (one-line JSON):
```json
{"claim_id":"","chunk_index":2,"chunk_count":4,"fingerprint":"abc123","meta":{"account":"acct-9","req_id":"abc123"}}
```
Ingest uses chunk_count to detect finalization and emits ledger writes after verifying dedupe.

ingest-bot: deploy:ingest-sidecar v2.10 deployed to staging at 5223456000 :rocket:

Tom: Edge case: gateway restart or multi-gateway replays generating different suggested claim_ids for same fingerprint. Ingest must maintain fingerprint->canonical_claim_id mapping and perform a CAS or upsert that returns canonical id. On conflict, return existing canonical id to caller.

Raj: Scaling note: the mapping table needs TTL/compaction policy. Keep hot mapping for 7 days, then compact to ledger reference. We'll need a compaction job that folds mapping into ledger rows and deletes mapping keys.

Lena: Observability: add a metric claim_reconciliation.counter and a sampled log line claim_resolution for reconciliations. Also add a sparse tracing tag on the ingest path with claim.origin and claim.resolved_by.

Sofia: Plan: I will update the gist with the handshake snippet + sample checkpoint format and open a tiny RFC linking the tests we should run (chunk replay, header loss, cross-gateway clash). Implementation plan: prototype mapping and reconciliation logic in the ingest sidecar (2w), integration tests (3d), staging rollout (1w).

Tom: :+1:

Raj: +1 on TTL and metrics. I'll add the compaction job sketch to the RFC.

Lena: Sounds good. If folks want to pair on the prototype ping me.

Sofia: Thanks all — will post RFC link shortly and tag reviewers.
